- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–3% to forecast to account for mean reversion toward prior range.
- Model overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; for 30-day forecasts, smooth transitions using 3–5 day moving average of sentiment-weighted history.
- When sentiment is mixed (alternating 0.33–0.67), model exhibits high volatility; cap forecast range within ±2% of 14-day moving average to avoid extreme outliers.
- If true outcome shows early mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 days after peak), model often fails to adjust; apply a “reversion bias” correction: reduce forecast by 1–4% for days 4–7 post-peak.
